info.title: Ungapped API
info.description: ## Introduction To use the Ungapped API you must first authenticate the current user and receive a token. All subsequent requests to the API should then provide the token. ## Authentication Create an API-Key in the account settings. Then pass it as x-api-key in the headers. ### Example ``` curl -X GET --header 'x-api-key: API-XXXXX' 'https://api.ungapped.com/Contacts' ``` ## Getting single objects Getting single objects usually follows the pattern /Objects/{ObjectId} where {ObjectId} is usually a GUID. So to get a list you get /Lists/{ListId}, to get a contact /Contacts/{ContactId} etc. You need to pass the x-api-key. If the authorization fails (perhaps expired) "401 Unauthorized" error is returned. If no object matching the id is found a "404 Not found"" error is returned. ### Example ``` curl -X GET --header 'x-api-key: API-XXXXX' 'https://api.ungapped.com/Contacts/12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456781234' ``` ## Getting multiple objects Getting multiple objects usually follows the pattern /Objects. So to get all lists you use /Lists, to get all contacts you use /Contacts etc. You need to pass the x-api-key. If the authorization fails (perhaps expired) "401 Unauthorized" error is returned. If no object matching the id is found an empty list is returned. ### Example ``` curl -X GET --header 'x-api-key: API-XXXXX' 'https://api.ungapped.com/Contacts' ``` ### OData for multiple results Most calls returning multiple results allow a limited set of OData query options for filtering, sorting, paging etc. Please read [Supporting OData Query Options](http://www.asp.net/web-api/overview/odata-support-in-aspnet-web-api/supporting-odata-query-options) for details. #### $select To limit the amount of data queried and sent over the network you should try to use the $select attribute. ``` /Contacts?$select=ContactId,FirstName,LastName ``` #### $filter To filter the results use the $filter attribute. ``` /Contacts?$filter=endswith(Email, '@gmail.com') ``` #### $top and $skip To implement paging use the $top and $skip attribute. ``` /Contacts?$top=10&$skip=10 ``` #### $orderby To implement sorting $orderby attribute. ``` /Contacts?$orderby=FirstName,LastName ``` ## Creating single object Creating an object usually follows the pattern POST new object to /Objects. So to create contact post a contact item to /Contacts. You need to pass the api-key. If the authorization fails (perhaps expired) "401 Unauthorized" error is returned. If the data passed is not valid a "400 Bad Request" error is returned. ### Example ``` curl -X POST --header 'x-api-key: API-XXXXX' -d '{ Email: %27oscar.uribe@ungapped.com%27, FirstName: %27Oscar%27, LastName: %27Uribe%27 }' 'https://api.ungapped.com/Contacts' ``` ## Updating single object Updating an object usually follows the pattern POST updated object to /Objects/{ObjectId}. So to update a contact post a contact item to /Contacts/{ContactId}. You need to pass the api-key. If the authorization fails (perhaps expired) "401 Unauthorized" error is returned. If no object matching the id is found a "404 Not found" error is returned. If the data passed is not valid a "400 Bad Request" error is returned. ###Example ``` curl -X POST --header 'x-api-key: API-XXXXX' -d '{ ContactId: %2712345678-1234-1234-1234-123456781234%27, Email: %27oscar.uribe@ungapped.com%27, FirstName: %27Oscar%27, LastName: %27Uribe%27 }' 'https://api.ungapped.com/Contacts/12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456781234' ``` ## Rate limit All API-calls are limited to a maximum number of calls per second. If the number of calls is exceeded an error will be returned: 409 The allowed number of requests has been exceeded. On all results two headers will be returned with how many calls are allowed and how many are remaining: ``` RateLimit-Limit: 50 RateLimit-Remaining: 33 ```
